tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.91.0 and v0.92.0 with the exact published command contract (Core 0.428.0, Base 0.57.0): the shared store moves to version 33; permissions are checked under each command's full key (messages.sync, bot.messages.sync) and a saved deny on either now stops the command; a saved permission key that names no command and the retired default_profile and analysis_* settings are refused with the config unset that removes them, while config show, set and unset still run; doctor --json lists every config problem in config.issues and reports a config file or folder other users can read under files with the chmod fix; config set keeps config.json at 0600; run records gain cli_command, agent and error; skill status, skill show --for and store tables list are new. RU/ES changed guides, changelog and technical reference reviewed. The native roadmap now drops bot button presses, chats start and chats app, so its portal correction was retired, as were the fixed MCP-guide lists (BUG-391), the removed search mail sentence and the analysis-setting option column; the generated reference has no empty Returns lists (BUG-392). The bot guide's --from start option is still corrected to --until-id. Chat notes, emoji reaction rankings, remaining max parity (privacy, calls, chat media, stickers, deleting or clearing a chat, group photo) and location remain planned.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.74.0 to v0.76.0 (0.75.0 and 0.76.0), release commit d8c2911072aa259c89e1d375ae36345c3f4367a7, Core 0.428.0/Base 0.57.0. Native Russian source and EN/ES translations cover config.json written owner-only (0600) with doctor naming a config file or folder others can read (files) and every settings-file problem with a runnable config unset fix (config.issues, replacing config.error); unknown and old settings (default_profile, analysis_*, MAX_ANALYSIS_*, camelCase names, the old allow list) and permission keys no command checks are refused until removed, while config show|set|unset still work to repair the file; messages sync permissions checked under their full key; MAX_INSTALL_AGENT as the only installer variable; skill status and skill show --for; store tables list; crash reported as internal_error. The roadmap is unchanged and none of its items shipped. The search correction for the removed mail hint was retired because 0.76.0 dropped the hint; the usage --all and mcp max_write corrections still apply to 0.76.0. Old-name checks and the doctor/config repair flow were run in an isolated sandbox with synthetic config files. No live account checks or extra release performed.

zm.conclusion: Reviewed Zoom0.36.0–0.42.0 with the exact published command contract, including permission discovery, unified search hit paging, review/mentions/saved searches, model and archive vocabulary, profile examples and keyring diagnostics. EN/RU/ES full guide and technical-reference review completed. Source Zoom#245 corrects older released security/search/usage/roadmap claims; explicit portal runtime errata preserve the reviewed0.42 grammar and discovery contract3 rather than importing newer Core411 behavior. Custom/team-authorized Zoomapp required; no public shared app promised. Audio recording of attended calls, notes/speaker naming, broader preparation and additional platforms remain planned.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed released Drive 0.34.0 (Core 0.422.0/Base 0.53.0). drive keeps a log of its runs like tg, max and wa: failed runs always, every run with --record or record: true in defaults, for keep_runs_for_days (30); runs list|show|path read them without a profile, and a run never holds a document id, name or text. Help and MCP examples speak of drive and name a profile. EN/RU/ES configuration (record, keep_runs_for_days, --record/--no-record), troubleshooting (failed-run symptom row), commands and changelog reviewed. Roadmap unchanged: Google app review in progress, background watch service and front matter next, larger annotation copies and mirror deletion later. Earlier: search --json hits carry cli-core's url and kind: "document", the same fields as memo search notes and search all; source_url is removed without an alias from hits and pictures, and a folder hit is told apart by not_read: "folder metadata only". An expired Google sign-in now tells an agent that signing in is the owner's step. EN/RU/ES search and usage now name url; the recipes and troubleshooting guide overrides (documents account, older-CLI refusal) are retired because 0.33.0 ships those pages. Roadmap unchanged from 0.32.0: Google app review in progress, background watch service and front matter next, larger annotation copies and mirror deletion later. Earlier review of 0.30.0 to 0.32.0: 0.32.0 keeps Drive documents in the store's own Google Drive account named by the drive profile; Core 0.420.0 moves them on first open (store versions 30 to 33), keeps every document:<id> reference, and older CLIs refuse the store until upgraded; two processes on one profile share a single Google sign-in refresh. 0.31.0 moves files list to the shared field query language (name:, modified_time with offsets, --timezone; raw Google queries stay under api), adds schema-derived list queries and joins a file's owner or editor with the mail contact of the same exact email. 0.30.0 removes mirrors sync/watch --public-url: Google Docs inserts only publicly downloadable images, so local images stay as Markdown text. EN/RU/ES mirrors (new section on when a Markdown file in Drive is enough; local images section rewritten), recipes (search only Drive documents from Memo with --source drive:<profile>), roadmap (tunnel image claim removed from the current summary), commands and changelog reviewed. Roadmap: background watch service and front matter stay next; larger annotation copies and mirror deletion stay later; Google app review stays in progress. The documents account and the older-CLI refusal reach the recipes and troubleshooting guides through docs-only guide overrides (drive PRs 220 and 222). No live Google request or global upgrade.

memo.conclusion: Reviewed Memo 0.94.0–0.97.0 with exact Core 0.414.0/Base 0.51.0. 0.97.0 adds authenticated HTTP MCP (MEMO-23) through Core’s shared transport, access-code OAuth and revocation, with the same three tools and per-call permissions as stdio; Core 0.414.0 supplies a positional and its flag alternative once, fixing note creation. Intervening releases add search people, Drive files in context, schema-derived list queries (protected:true replaces --filter is:protected), linked-chat caps in project evidence, the inherited --topic-name selector and WhatsApp as a store source. EN/RU/ES remote, MCP, security, index, roadmap, people, search, mail, archive, configuration, how-it-works, usage, generated reference and 0.94–0.97 release notes reviewed; the released changelog has no 0.95.0 section (cli-memo source issue, not corrected here). Roadmap: HTTP moved to current; nothing under Next or Later shipped. 660 synthetic runtime tests pass; no owner data, live tunnel or paid API use.

wa.conclusion: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.7.0 and v0.8.0 with the exact published command contract and package: invite previews (chats inspect), linked-device ids (account sessions list), custom Lists read from synced labels (chats folders list|show; folder writes stay refused), received community comments (messages comments; channels have none, sending stays unavailable), canonical shared command names without aliases, query-based search runs and bot templates list, item/end watch JSONL, permission-denied commands discoverable with availability, and mcp.authority / bot.api gating over MCP. RU/ES changed guides, changelog and technical reference reviewed. Native v0.8.0 moved Cloud API bots and verified attachment archives to current capabilities, so the whole-page roadmap correction was retired. Narrow source-linked errata remain: the roadmap and usage guide dropped old-file downloads although the released attachments guide and media.retry-failed still document the limitation, and the MCP terminal-only list was rebuilt from the 0.8.0 contract. Channel files, business labels, the guide command, broader albums, communities and sent-reaction storage remain planned.
